title: Crowdsearch
abstract: arXiv:2311.08532v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A common economic process is crowdsearch, wherein a group of agents is invited to search for a valuable object, such as a software vulnerability or a proof-of-work nonce. We study a binary model of crowdsearch in which agents with heterogeneous search costs decide whether or not to search. Inviting more agents directly expands the pool of potential searchers, but it also increases competition for the prize and lowers individual search incentives. This crowding-out effect may dominate, so that inviting more agents can lower the probability of finding the object. We show that inviting an unlimited crowd need not guarantee success. We also provide sufficient conditions, based on the lower-tail behavior of the cost distribution, under which the probability of success is eventually increasing or eventually decreasing in the number of agents.

translated_abstract: 众包搜索是一种常见的经济过程，即邀请一群代理人去寻找有价值的对象，例如软件漏洞或工作量证明随机数。我们研究了众包搜索的一个二元模型，其中具有异质搜索成本的代理人自行决定是否参与搜索。邀请更多的代理人直接扩大了潜在搜索者的范围，但同时也加剧了对奖励的竞争并削弱了个体的搜索激励。这种挤出效应可能占据主导地位，从而导致邀请更多代理人反而会降低找到目标对象的概率。我们证明，邀请无限规模的人群并不一定能保证搜索成功。此外，我们基于成本分布的下尾行为，给出了成功概率最终随代理人数量递增或递减的充分条件。
tldr: 论文通过异质搜索成本下“是否搜索”的二元决策模型发现，邀请更多代理人会因竞争加剧而挤出个体搜索激励，甚至降低找到目标的概率，并基于成本分布的下尾行为给出了成功概率最终递增或递减的充分条件。
en_tdlr: Using a binary model where agents with heterogeneous search costs decide whether to search, the paper shows that inviting more agents can crowd out individual incentives and even lower the probability of finding the object, and it provides sufficient conditions based on the lower tail of the cost distribution under which the success probability is eventually increasing or decreasing in the number of agents.
